open_points.subject: A8 / EXIF date parsing
open_points.question: Must a raw `DateTimeOriginal` or `DateTime` value match this pattern in full, and must the matched components also form a valid calendar date and time?
options: Require a full-string match and reject calendar-invalid component values as malformed
Use a prefix or substring match, then parse the matched part
Leave recognition and calendar validation to the image library
open_points.default_guess: Require a full-string match and strict calendar validation; otherwise treat the camera value as unusable.

witness.initial: A source has `DateTimeOriginal` equal to `2026:11:20 10:20:30junk` and a usable modification time with a different instant.
events: The calling flow requests placement of the source.
The deliverer chooses the first usable photo moment.
outcomes: A full match rejects the EXIF value and uses the modification time.
A prefix match accepts the EXIF value and uses 2026-11-20 10:20:30.
witness.observer: The caller sees a different `photo_date` and `date_source` in the placement.

open_points.subject: A8 / EXIF offset parsing
open_points.question: Is this pattern required to match `OffsetTimeOriginal` in full before the separate hour and minute bounds are checked, or is some other interpretation of the string allowed?
options: Full-match the imported pattern, then enforce the hour and minute bounds
Accept a matching prefix or a value normalized by the image library
Use the prose `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM` rule without reading this constant
open_points.default_guess: Full-match the imported pattern and then enforce the stated bounds.

witness.initial: A source has a valid `DateTimeOriginal`, `OffsetTimeOriginal` equal to `+02:00junk`, and the run time zone has a different UTC offset.
events: The deliverer interprets the camera time.
outcomes: A full match rejects the offset and interprets the camera time in the run time zone.
A prefix match accepts `+02:00` and converts the camera time using that offset.
witness.observer: The caller sees a different UTC `photo_date`.

open_points.subject: A8 / M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: Which authority supplies `marked_at`, at what event is it read, is it represented as naive UTC or offset-aware time, and how many clock readings may a new or replayed mark operation take?
options: The service clock is read once when a new mark is durably created; store naive UTC, and do not read it on replay
The service clock is read when the mark request begins
The persistence backend supplies the instant when it commits
open_points.default_guess: Read the service clock once immediately before creating the durable mark, store naive UTC, and preserve the stored value without a clock read on replay.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a publication mark; a mark request begins at 10:00:00 and its durable write completes at 10:00:05.
events: The owner's calling flow submits the Portal photo id.
The deliverer creates the publication mark.
The same mark is later read or replayed.
outcomes: `marked_at` is 10:00:00 because the operation reads the clock at request entry.
`marked_at` is 10:00:05 because the operation reads the clock at durable creation.
witness.observer: A check or repository reader inspecting the persisted or replayed mark sees the difference.

open_points.subject: A2 / file modification time
open_points.text: A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
open_points.question: Must one placement read the file's modification time exactly once and use that same instant both for camera-time plausibility and as the fallback photo moment?
options: Read it once and reuse that reading throughout the operation
Read it independently for the plausibility comparison and for fallback
Use whichever modification time accompanies each filesystem or image-library operation
open_points.default_guess: Read the modification time once and reuse the same value for every decision in that placement.

witness.initial: The camera time is 25 hours after the file's initial modification time and 23 hours after a later modification time.
events: The deliverer reads the initial modification time.
Another actor changes the file's modification time while placement is running.
The deliverer checks camera plausibility and chooses the photo moment.
outcomes: With one reading, the camera value is unusable and the initial modification time is used.
With a later rereading, the camera value is usable and becomes the photo moment.
witness.observer: The caller sees a different `photo_date` and `date_source`.

open_points.subject: A2 / file modification time representation
open_points.text: A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
open_points.question: When the filesystem modification instant has sub-second precision, must that precision be preserved, rounded, or truncated in `taken_at` and `photo_date`, and is the resulting UTC datetime naive or offset-aware before delivery?
options: Preserve all precision representable by `datetime` and deliver naive UTC
Truncate to whole seconds to match EXIF precision
Preserve an offset-aware UTC datetime internally and remove the offset only in the publication body
open_points.default_guess: Preserve representable microseconds and use naive UTC consistently in `taken_at` and `photo_date`.

witness.initial: A source has no usable camera time and has a modification instant of 2026-11-20T10:20:30.500000Z.
events: The deliverer falls back to the modification time and builds the publication body.
outcomes: The delivered value is truncated or rounded to whole seconds.
witness.observer: The caller and Portal see different `photo_date` values.
